narrative.overview:
Packman is a tool, not a page. UI mode should read as something that shipped with VS Code: it takes its colors, fonts and focus behavior from the host and adds none of its own. Nothing here has a fixed hex value; every color is a `--vscode-*` token, so the same markup is correct in any light, dark or high-contrast theme, in VS Code and in Cursor.

The density is that of an editor panel: a single left-aligned column up to 60rem, headed by the package's own `name@version` with Refresh and Edit mode beside it, small uppercase section labels, key/value pairs and tables that read like the file they summarize. Hierarchy comes from weight, case and the theme's muted foreground, not from size jumps or ornament. The one place the system lets itself be more present is the Script button, which is built to be pressed and answers the press.
keyCharacteristics: No colors, fonts or icons of its own: theme tokens only.
Editor-panel density, one column, max 60rem; the package name is the title.
Muted labels, full-strength values; data in the editor font.
Flat at rest; structure from 1px theme borders, never shadows.
Script buttons are tactile: they have a visible hover, a pressed state and a focus ring.
Missing data is stated plainly (muted, warning, or error tokens), never guessed.
Dependency rows give a verdict in words (`major`, `alerts`, "2 need attention"), not raw numbers alone.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: Never write a hex, rgb or hsl color in UI mode. If a role has no token, find the nearest `--vscode-*` token and give it a fallback chain.

rules.name: The Not-Color-Alone Rule
rules.body: Status is never carried by color alone: every status is a word (`major`, `alerts`, `paused`, `offline`, `timed out`), and color only reinforces it.

rules.name: The No-Fade Rule
rules.body: Never dim text with `opacity`. Use the muted token; opacity on top of it fails contrast.

rules.name: The Host Size Rule
rules.body: Body size is whatever `--vscode-font-size` says. Scale everything else in `em` from there (`rem` is the browser's 16px, not the editor's), never compound `em` below 11px, and keep the hierarchy within a narrow range.

rules.name: The Name Gets the Slack Rule
rules.body: In any table, the first column is the one that flexes; every other column has a fixed width shared across tables. When the name would get too narrow, the table stacks instead of crushing it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. If something needs to stand out, change its fill or border token, not its elevation.

dos: Do use only `--vscode-*` tokens for color, with a fallback chain where a token may be absent.
Do put data in the editor font and labels in the UI font.
Do keep the 4px radius and 1px hairline borders everywhere, with a `0.75rem` inset between text and any border.
Do update a live page with the `render` message, not by reassigning `webview.html`, so scroll, focus and open sections survive.
Do give every interactive element a `:focus-visible` outline in `--vscode-focusBorder`.
Do state missing or paused data in words (muted, warning, or error tokens), and keep the layout stable when it happens.
Do verify any change in a light, a dark and a high-contrast theme.
donts: Don't introduce a brand color, a custom typeface, an icon font or an image asset.
Don't add shadows, gradients, glows or rounded pills.
Don't make UI mode editable; edits belong in Edit mode.
Don't convey status by color alone, and don't dim text with `opacity`.
Don't let the page scroll horizontally; scroll wide content inside its own wrapper.
Don't make UI mode look like a webpage in the editor: no hero areas, no marketing type scale, no centered layouts.
